paragraphs.source_en: Toyotomi Hideyoshi arrived at Osaka Castle in early September of the second year of Bunroku. Along the familiar banks of the Yodo River, the reeds and silver-grass plumes had begun to whiten. The people of Osaka, whose lives were growing more prosperous by the day, vied with one another to come out and welcome him, and the festive mood approached frenzy. Hideyoshi assumed an air of great delight, making people think he rejoiced over the truce and peace negotiations and the birth of his son; inwardly, however, he felt nothing of the kind.

paragraphs.source_en: As for the peace negotiations, the Ming envoys had indeed departed Nagoya carrying the seven conditions put forward by Hideyoshi. Japan had also sent Konishi Yukinaga's father, Joan, to the Ming capital of Beijing and asked Shen Weijing to sound out the situation. In the end, however, they discovered that matters were not as promising as imagined—both sides were playing a game of deception.

paragraphs.source_en: Shortly after the Hour of the Sheep, Hideyoshi entered Osaka Castle. Having quickly disposed of his public business, he hurried into the inner quarters. He had intended, the moment he entered the castle, to have Chacha bring Ohiro from the western compound and then speak face-to-face with Hidetsugu and the others. But Hidetsugu had ruthlessly shattered that dream of familial bliss. Hideyoshi knew full well that if, upon returning, he did nothing but hold and kiss Ohiro, Hidetsugu would suffer all the more when word reached him.
